documentTypes.title: model
documentTypes.summary: a model built from code and held in the engine's memory, with no file behind it: addressed by its document id (cad run SCRIPT.py prints it) or the handle its call returns

operations.name: export
operations.summary: write the document to other files, each kind by its suffix (.step, .glb, .stl, .3mf, .dxf, .xbf, .xml (MJCF, its meshes beside it), .urdf (its meshes beside it)); --tolerance and --angle mesh a .glb, an .stl or a .3mf finer

operations.name: snapshot
operations.summary: draw it as the viewer does, into a PNG

operations.name: inspect
operations.summary: what the document holds, then its build closure; with a ref, what one element or part is and what made it

operations.name: dfm
operations.summary: check it can be made: CNC machining (--process cnc), sheet metal (sheet), injection molding (molding) or 3D printing (printing), measured and judged against general, cited rules, each finding at a face's or an edge's ref

operations.name: interference
operations.summary: which parts share volume, as built and at each pose asked (--pose: a mechanism state, a configuration sequence at a time, or joint values): a pair with air between its parts ruled out on their meshes, every other measured exactly on the parts' own solids, the fits named on purpose (--fit A B) listed apart, and each pair it could not measure said

operations.name: solve
operations.summary: a linear static stress study of a part or a bonded assembly: with --study and --out DIR, the solve, its results written into DIR (result.json, result.glb, result.vtu, stress.png, displacement.png), each part's peak stress and safety factor, and a part that yields failing it; with no --study, the parts, the pairs that touch and a part's faces a study names

operations.name: ranges
operations.summary: each joint's stops found from the geometry: the joint turned or slid alone, a step at a time each way, until its parts meet another part; the stops and which parts meet, nothing written

producers.accepts: a build123d Shape a model returns

documentTypes.title: KiCad PCB
documentTypes.summary: a KiCad printed circuit board, read with the .kicad_pro beside it

operations.name: export
operations.summary: write its fabrication and 3D outputs with KiCad into a folder: gerbers, drill, pos, bom, step, glb, odb, ipc2581, pdf or dxf

operations.name: snapshot
operations.summary: draw it flat, as the viewer's board view does, into a PNG

operations.name: inspect
operations.summary: what the board holds: its format, thickness, size, layers, parts and nets

operations.name: drc
operations.summary: KiCad's design rule check: errors and unconnected items fail it, warnings are said

edit.hands: the open board, through KiCad's IPC API (kicode's KiPy)

documentTypes.title: KiCad schematic
documentTypes.summary: a KiCad schematic, read with every sheet of its project's hierarchy

operations.name: export
operations.summary: write it with KiCad: a pdf, an svg per sheet, the netlist or a BOM, into a folder

operations.name: snapshot
operations.summary: draw one sheet flat, as KiCad's schematic editor shows it, into a PNG

operations.name: inspect
operations.summary: what the schematic holds: its sheets, parts and nets; with a ref, what that names

operations.name: erc
operations.summary: KiCad's electrical rules check: errors fail it, warnings are said

edit.hands: the open schematic, its project's symbol libraries loaded, through KiCad's IPC API (kicode's KiPy)

integrations.name: build123d
integrations.summary: build123d and the OCCT kernel under it (OCP): model code builds with it, and the engine makes, reads, writes and draws documents with it

integrations.name: kicad
integrations.summary: KiCad's command line, kicad-cli, and its IPC API, both kicode's: a board's design rule check and its fabrication exports run kicad-cli, headless, and an edit of a board or a schematic goes through the API

integrations.name: trimesh
integrations.summary: trimesh, the triangle-mesh library: a mesh's manufacturing check measures it with trimesh for 3D printing -- its walls, overhangs and support; every other process is judged on exact geometry

integrations.name: mujoco
integrations.summary: MuJoCo, the physics engine, as its headless core (mujoco-core: the compiler and the bindings, no renderer) and MuJoCo Studio's web viewer: cad.mujoco makes a document a mujoco.MjSpec, chooses a part's collision on it and saves it; `cad mujoco check robot.xml` compiles a MuJoCo model with the core, so what MuJoCo refuses is a finding with MuJoCo's own words; and `cad run mujoco-studio --model scene.xml` serves the model in Studio for the person to open in a browser

operations.name: check
operations.summary: compile a MuJoCo model (an MJCF) with MuJoCo and check it: what MuJoCo refuses or warns of, the model-health checks, what collides as what, and the contact excludes

integrations.holds: MuJoCo's headless core and MuJoCo Studio

integrations.name: coacd
integrations.summary: CoACD, the approximate convex decomposition of a triangle mesh: cad.mujoco.decompose makes a part of a MuJoCo function's spec collide as the convex hulls CoACD cuts its mesh into, its visual whole, always in a process of its own (its TBB and the kernel's cannot share one), the hulls kept in the engine's cache by the mesh's digest

integrations.name: netgen
integrations.summary: netgen, the tetrahedral mesher: a stress study (solve) meshes a part's own faces with it, curved second-order elements, every face kept under its ref, always in a process of its own (its OpenCascade and the kernel's cannot share one)

integrations.name: calculix
integrations.summary: CalculiX's solver, ccx, as the cad-ccx package carries it: a stress study (solve) writes its input, runs it headless on one thread in a private folder, and reads its answer

integrations.name: blender
integrations.summary: Blender as a Python module, bpy (the Blender Foundation's wheel): a script loads the GLB cad exports into Blender's scene, every part where the file places it and each clip playable alone (cad.blender.load), then frames, lights and renders it with bpy itself
